title: Engagement with self-management apps among adults with epilepsy: a scoping review
abstract: Objective: to map how engagement with epilepsy self-management apps is defined, measured and sustained, which features and clinician support accompany sustained use, which outcomes are reported alongside engagement, and who does not engage. Design: scoping review following JBI guidance, reported with PRISMA-ScR. Results will be charted by June 2027.
introduction: Clinics recommend self-management apps, but engagement decays within months, is measured inconsistently and has not been linked to seizure outcomes in trials.
methods: Searches of four databases, two app-evaluation repositories and charity websites by the library; dual screening; charting verified by a second reviewer; outcomes charted as associations.
results: No charting has been done yet. The report will present the PRISMA-ScR flow diagram and maps of definitions, engagement over time, features and support, outcomes and access.
discussion: The discussion will state what the map means for choosing between nurse coaching and a hospital-built app.
limitations: English only; incompatible engagement definitions; favourable commercial reports.
conclusion: To be written after charting; it will describe the field and not estimate effects.
summary: PRISMA-ScR draft with results left empty until charting.
